Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood integration anomaly observed — need IRP and artifacts

Marcus —

We observed a spike in failed callbacks coming from Redwood's webhook for our payments reconciliation job between 07:02–07:08 PDT this morning. That window corresponds to a batch of customer payouts that were retried three times; some customer payouts were delayed.

We haven't seen evidence of data exfiltration but our security team is treating this as an operational security event and is requesting the following from Redwood immediately:

- A copy of Redwood's incident response plan (IRP) or a pointer to the portion that covers service interruptions and third-party integrations.
- Any retained telemetry and request/response logs for the 07:00–07:15 PDT window (redacted as needed).
- A short timeline of what your team saw and any mitigations applied.

Please mark this high priority — legal and procurement may open an evidence request ticket.

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Security Operations
Acme Payments

Subject: Re: Redwood integration anomaly observed — need IRP and artifacts

Marcus / Lydia —

I dug into the runtime logs for the timeframe Marcus mentioned. Quick summary for internal: there was a transient increase in retry/backpressure signals on our webhook delivery queue caused by an upstream S3 throttling event affecting a pickled cache shard; the retry loop caused a bunch of 502s to be returned to your webhook consumer. No indicators of lateral movement or data egress in the telemetry we currently have.

Lydia, for the formal evidence packet, please let us know if you need: SIG questionnaire items (we can fill the relevant subset), CAIQ references, or raw/processed logs. To make this usable for procurement/legal we typically provide: 
- IRP excerpt (actions we take on detected delivery failures and third-party integration escalation).
- Delivery logs: request_id, timestamp, status_code, latency_ms (we can provide CSV with redacted payloads).
- Service health snapshot and autoscaling events for the 07:00–07:30 PDT window.
- A statement of no evidence of data exfiltration (if you need a signed attestation we can do that via your procurement contact).

Proposed timeline: 
- 09:00–10:00 PDT: internal forensic extraction and redaction check.
- 10:00 PDT: share a sanitized telemetry sample + IRP excerpt (PDF).
- 14:00 PDT: deliver the fuller SIG/CAIQ crosswalk or schedule a quick call to go over it.

Please confirm whether the sanitized sample is acceptable or if you need the full unredacted logs (we would request an NDA for raw packets).

Naomi Feldman
Senior Security Engineer, Incident Response
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood integration anomaly observed — evidence delivery (sanitized sample + IRP excerpt)

Lydia —

Per Naomi's timeline, attached are two artifacts for your triage team: 
- redwood-IRP-summary.pdf (PDF, 420KB) — excerpted IRP section covering third-party integration failures and escalation chains.
- redwood-telemetry-sample.csv (CSV, 280KB) — sanitized delivery logs for 2025-07-21T07:00:00–2025-07-21T07:30:00 PDT. Fields: request_id, timestamp_utc, status_code, latency_ms, endpoint. Payloads were removed or hashed.

We uploaded the same set to a secure folder for procurement/legal: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d_secure_acme_exchange (link expires in 14 days). HubSpot ticket created: HSP-789210.

Actions we took: 
- 07:09 PDT: identified S3 throttling event and promoted a fallback shard.
- 07:11 PDT: scaled additional workers and drained backlog; delivery success rate returned to baseline by 07:25 PDT.
- 08:30 PDT: ran a controlled re-replay of a sample batch to confirm corrected behavior.

If you need the unredacted logs for a particular payment_id list you provide, we will request an evidence-access agreement (NDA) before delivery.

Let me know the preferred next step — quick sync call or a written SIG/CAIQ crosswalk later today.

Best,
Marcus
